claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse and microstructurally heterogeneous near-surface region.
Ultrasonic burnishing will generate an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Ultrasonic burnishing will homogenize the coating's near-surface microstructure.
The burnishing-induced ultra-nanocrystalline layer will be maintained during sliding at approximately 600°C.
Ultrasonic burnishing introduces severe plastic deformation into the coating surface.
The severe plastic deformation caused by ultrasonic burnishing refines the surface grain structure.
Burnishing-induced grain refinement facilitates dynamic recrystallization.
The refined near-surface structure shifts the dominant deformation mode from dislocation slip toward grain-boundary-mediated deformation.
A shift toward grain-boundary-mediated deformation reduces localized strain concentrations.
Reduced localized strain concentrations mitigate abrasive wear.
The ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer promotes more homogeneous microscopic deformation during high-temperature sliding.
At approximately 600°C, the burnished coating will have a lower friction coefficient than the untreated coating under otherwise identical sliding conditions.
At approximately 600°C, the burnished coating will have lower wear volume than the untreated coating under otherwise identical sliding conditions.
The burnished coating will exhibit increased grain-boundary sliding relative to the untreated coating.
The burnished coating will exhibit fewer dislocation pile-ups than the untreated coating.
The predicted improvements are limited to high-temperature sliding near 600°C at controlled load and sliding speed.
Long-term thermal stability of the burnishing-induced ultra-nanocrystalline layer during sustained high-temperature sliding is uncertain.
